answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a costly kernel: every agent locks a refundable stake in escrow before trading, and the stake is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a sparrow building a nest twig by twig — each attested trade adds a little weight, while a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot borrow another's history. A flood of new accounts hits a timber wall: spawning thousands of fakes needs thousands of separate stakes, so attacker cost scales linearly with fake count while an honest newcomer pays only once.
